problem.text: Hexadecimal (base-$16$) numbers are written using numeric digits $0$ through $9$ as well as the letters $A$ through $F$ to represent $10$ through $15$. Among the first $1000$ positive integers, there are $n$ whose hexadecimal representation contains only numeric digits. What is the sum of the digits of $n$?

steps.title: Where to start: write $1000$ in base $16$
steps.body: The condition is about hexadecimal digits, but the limit $1000$ is given in base $10$. To see which hex digit strings stay at or below the limit, first write the limit itself in base $16$. The place values are $16^2 = 256$, $16^1 = 16$ and $16^0 = 1$.

your_turn.answer: $1000 = 3\cdot 256 + 14\cdot 16 + 8$, so it is $3E8_{16}$ (the digit $14$ is written $E$).

steps.title: Which digit strings are allowed
steps.body: Every number up to $1000$ has at most three hex digits, so write each one as a three-digit string, padding with leading zeros. The first digit can only be $0$, $1$, $2$ or $3$, because a first digit of $4$ already means at least $4\cdot 256 = 1024$. The other two digits must be numeric, so each is $0$ through $9$.

your_turn.prompt: The largest such string is $399_{16}$. Is it below $1000$?
your_turn.answer: Yes: $3\cdot 256 + 9\cdot 16 + 9 = 921$. So every string with first digit $0$ to $3$ and other digits $0$ to $9$ is inside the range.

steps.title: Count the strings
steps.body: Now count by choices: $4$ options for the first digit and $10$ for each of the other two. Careful: one of these strings is $000$, which stands for the number $0$, and $0$ is not one of the first $1000$ positive integers.

your_turn.prompt: How many three-digit strings are there in total, before removing anything?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Removing the string $000$ leaves $n = 400 - 1 = 399$ positive integers whose hex form uses only numeric digits. The sum of the digits of $n$ is $3 + 9 + 9 = 21$. The answer is **(E)** $21$.
